MAPE divides each absolute error by the actual value, becoming undefined at zero and unstable near zero. For the common $sMAPE=2|y-\hat y|/(|y|+|\hat y|)$, exchanging actual and forecast is symmetric, but equal over/under errors around a fixed positive actual have different denominators: for actual 100, forecasts 120 and 80 score about 18.2% and 22.2%. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

WMAPE, usually $\sum|y-\hat y|/\sum|y|$, avoids individual zero denominators but fails when the aggregate denominator is zero and emphasizes large-volume items. MASE divides MAE by training-set naive or seasonal-naive MAE, allowing scale comparisons; it fails when that reference error is zero. State the exact convention, aggregate carefully, and align the metric with business costs rather than assuming a percentage error is always interpretable.
